A1_S3_D1_1: ^The three of you make your way further into the forest, where the trees grow thicker and another ruin appears ahead.
^Amaya stops walking and gestures for you to go forward.
^You got past a puzzle before we ran into each other, right? Show me how you did it.
secondpuzzle: ^Those are solid stone. It takes ten average men to move it manually.
^(It was quite heavy, but how does that make sense?)
^I guess someone like me must not be common around here?
^No, but this lady’s pretty strange, too!
completed_quest_1: ^So you really can move them on your own…
^I know you Krakenfolk are strong, but I didn’t realize it’d be to this extent.
^Yeah. I might be a Viridi, but I do talk to others too.
^(Maybe… there are others like me? Ones that also look like ‘monsters?’)
^You said that you’re here for a boat?
^Ah, yes! We were just looking for wood and other materials to fix it up.
^Truth be told, while you were familiar with building ships and the like, you’ve never chopped down whole trees, before.
^I… guess you might be able to tell, but I’m not from this island.
^So any help would be greatly appreciated.
^…Are you just recruiting anyone you see?
^You hush the dragon. It doesn’t hurt to ask!
^And intimidating as she may appear, the fact that this person hasn’t attacked you directly should indicate something.
^I won’t make any promises, but to make sure you aren’t a threat, I’ll need you to come with me to our settlement.
^Whether or not any of us will ‘help,’ depends on our leader’s judgement.
^The Viridi settlement is hidden amidst the forest, with small houses that make up a lively village.
^It’s certainly not as large as the community on your home island, but the appearance of so many people—Viridi—in one place, helps you relax a little.
^It’s a small piece of familiarity within the craziness of the past twenty-four hours, yet foreign at the same time.
^I found them outside, after they passed through the ruins.
^(...I guess the ruins were supposed to keep outsiders away.)
^Their methods and backstory seemed suspicious, so I brought them here.
^I need to speak to the Elder, so can you keep watch, Chione?
^Hey! We’re not some kind of dangerous animal!
^The two smoothly move past the comment and continue.
^Once Amaya has made her leave, Chione introduces herself to break the ice.
silenttochione: ^…Oh, it’s alright! You don’t need to be afraid to talk.
^Amaya’s actually a really nice person! She’s just protective of us.
^Trailing off, the curiosity in Chione’s eyes pushes her forward.
^What brought you to this island, if you don’t mind me asking?
introtochione: ^I’m Noelle Tempest, and this is Amelia.
^Tempest? That’s an interesting last name; so you’re not from this island?
^(So instead of my appearance, it’s my last name that gives that away?)
meetchione: ^I got shipwrecked here this morning, and need to find a way to fix my boat.
^Fix your boat? Well you couldn’t have come at a better or worse time.
^Well… on one hand, we have plenty of wood you could use around here. But on the other, the Great Disaster’s almost ready to approach.
^The stories you’ve heard about the Great Floods from your home have always been quite vague.
^All you know is that they’re the reason your people have specialised in building arks; to sail through the floods, rather than allowing them to demolish everything you’ve built.
^But over here, everyone’s been referring to not the floods, but the creature behind it?
^Well… fixing my boat is my own way of preparing for the floods.
^If there’s a way to avoid it, shouldn’t that be done?
^The phrasing of your words causes concern to crease on Chione’s brow.
^I understand where you’re coming from, but please be careful of what you say around the village.
^It’s a brave thing to want to stop fate, but our way of life prioritises nature.
^Therefore, we shouldn’t mess with the natural order of things, or attempt to place our personal feelings above them.
^Our elder Silas has always taught us to respect the land; from the largest creatures to the smallest plants.
^Chione catches herself, trying to lighten the mood.
^…Which is why even allowing you to harvest wood in our area requires a green-light from him.
^I hope you understand; we only take as much as we need, and regularly give back to the island just as it helps us.
^But enough about that— I can still ‘keep an eye’ on you even when we aren’t talking, so feel free to explore around.
^Maybe even listen to Oren’s stories, while you’re at it! I’ll catch you later once arrangements are confirmed with Amaya and Silas.
^The weather has really gotten worse lately, it’s been raining so much!
^I hope it stops soon before it affects the forest.
^I wonder where Chione has been going off to lately; she says she’s been searching for herbs?
^Where were you yesterday? You missed the finale of Oren’s story.
^What happens? Do they get together in the end?
^They do, and get this— he ended up confessing to Noah!
^(Judging by how invested they sound, maybe it’d be a good idea to listen to this ‘Oren’s stories, too.)
^A settlement’s tales always reveal their culture, after all.
^Uh… but what was that about a confession?
^I overheard Oren talking to Silas earlier. I think today’s session will be about the Great Disaster!
^Before you an eavesdrop more, the two viridi villagers notice you.
^What’s a Krakenfolk doing so deep in the woods?
whatskraken: ^Don’t be silly, your features are pretty obvious.
^What are you doing in our village? You guys don’t tend to visit these parts.
^I was just looking for some simple supplies.
justsupplies: ^Well, you’ve come to the right place! Have you talked to Chione yet?
^Lovely! Oh and make sure to have a listen of Oren’s stories while you’re here. I think the session’s about to start.
^Right… I’ve been hearing about him. Who is Oren?
^He’s our local storyteller! Hosts shows very often based on some history and other made-up things.
